status_summary: The US has not recognized Somaliland. After Israel recognized it on 2025-12-26, the President said on 2025-12-27 that the US would not immediately follow and would study the matter. A State Department report to Congress posted on 2026-06-01 reaffirmed Somalia's sovereignty and territorial integrity, did not recommend changing recognition policy, and described ways to expand engagement with Somaliland, and in September 2026 Somaliland's president visited Washington without a reported change in the US position. A House bill (H.R. 3992, introduced 2025-06-12) would authorize the President to recognize Somaliland. On the wider China aim, a US-DRC strategic partnership signed 2025-12-04 gives US persons first-offer rights on Congolese strategic mineral projects and promotes the Sakania-Lobito corridor, though the summary read does not mention China; no digital-hygiene program was found.

timeline.event: H.R. 3992, the Republic of Somaliland Independence Act, was introduced and referred to the House Foreign Affairs Committee; it would authorize, not require, the President to recognize Somaliland.

The US and the Democratic Republic of the Congo signed a strategic partnership agreement on critical minerals, infrastructure and governance, with first-offer rights for US persons; the policy text does not mention China.
The President said the US would not immediately follow Israel's recognition of Somaliland and that he would study it.

State posted a report to Congress, titled Potential Areas for Improved United States Engagement with Somaliland and reported as required under the FY2026 appropriations act, that reaffirmed Somalia's sovereignty and territorial integrity, noted Somaliland's security and port value, and did not recommend changing US recognition policy.
Somaliland's president arrived in Washington seeking closer ties and recognition; Ahram Online reported that the US has maintained its position on Somaliland's status.

title: Counter Chinese activity in Africa, including recognizing Somaliland statehood
uncertainties: The State report itself was not read; its content and statutory basis come from three news accounts that agree (allAfrica, Middle East Eye and Somaliland Chronicle), and a search did not locate the report on state.gov. H.R. 3992's status was checked only through its introduced text, not a current congress.gov action list. The DRC agreement summary is from the IEA policy database, not the signed text. Other Africa activities (public diplomacy, digital security programs) were searched only briefly, and the Djibouti basing situation was not examined. Inference: the stage stays proposed because the specific measure (recognition) exists only as a bill and the general measures found are parallel; a reader could argue for a low in_progress rating on the DRC minerals agreement.
